newsitem.title: USA: U.S. utilities seen enjoying little user loyalty.
newsitem.headline: U.S. utilities seen enjoying little user loyalty.

text.p: Plans for electric utilities and new players like power marketers to develop brand loyalty for products and services may yield only limited success, industry analysts and officials said Tuesday.

"Loyalty is limited...Brand identity is difficult to establish for new players," said John E. Roberts, chief executive of South Wales Electricity plc, referring to early results of utility deregulation in the United Kingdom.

Speaking at the annual Edison Electric Institute convention here, Roberts said it has been difficult for power distribution companies like South Wales to sell value added services to industrial and large commercial customers.
He said UK consumers have been very ready to switch distribution companies to shop for the best deal.
UK began privatizing its electric utility industry in 1989.

In light of the loyalty experience in the UK, "it's a questionable premise (for U.S. power players) at this point," said Thomas Flaherty, national partner of utilities consulting at Deloitte & Touche.
Flaherty said it may still be too early in the deregulation of the U.S. utility industry for companies to develop brand name and loyalty for their products and services.

But Powergen plc director of international affairs Edgar McCarthy told Reuters, "You can build customer loyalty. You must provide services such as tailored billing and energy efficiency programs. We're building a brand image right now."

McCarthy noted Powergen, an electricity generator, is in a different competitive position than a power distribution company because it is an entity created under deregulation whereas distribution companies always existed in the UK.
"We had to come out fresh. The distributors always dealt with customers," said McCarthy.
